meta.title: CMSG — Computational Materials Science Group
meta.description: The Computational Materials Science Group at Soochow University studies materials with physics-based simulation, data, and machine learning.

intro.label: The Laboratory
intro.title: CMSG brings physics, data, and materials design into one unified working practice.
intro.body: Based in the School of Energy and the Soochow Institute of Energy and Materials Innovations (SIEMIS) at Soochow University, we develop computational methodologies, interatomic potentials, and open-source tools to tackle complex materials problems with clarity and precision.

research.label: Research Thrusts
research.title: Pioneering research pillars bridging atomic physics and macroscopic function.
research.subtitle: We tackle challenging problems in energy materials and condensed matter physics using first-principles calculations and AI.

items.title: Materials inverse design
items.summary: Start with a target property. Search across composition and crystal structure to discover materials with physics-informed machine learning.
items.image_alt: Materials inverse-design and machine-learning optimization framework

items.title: Physical discovery. Interpretable AI.
items.summary: Connect atomic structure to macroscopic behavior. Explore the physics behind superhard compounds and unusual thermal expansion.

items.title: Materials synthesizability & synthesis planning
items.summary: From whether a material can be synthesized to how. Combine physical similarity, experimental evidence, and language models to assess candidate routes, select precursors, and plan processing conditions.
items.image_alt: PIRAG-LM synthesis planning: chemical, structural, and thermodynamic precedents inform precursors, processing conditions, and interpretable synthesizability assessments
